title: Postmortem-to-Automated-Playbook Conversion Retrospective
author: Priya Rangan
content:
Overview

This retrospective summarizes the 6-month program to convert high-fidelity postmortems into automated, operator-facing runbooks ("playbooks"). The goal was to reduce mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for LLM inference incidents by replacing ad hoc operator procedures with deterministic, tested automation and decision artifacts.

Summary and outcome

- Program start: 2025-11-01 (pilot).
- Scope: 28 postmortems identified as repeatable incident classes across platform, runtime, and capacity layers.
- Outcome: 22 automated playbooks shipped to production, 4 operator-runbooks (manual steps retained), 2 deferred for further instrumentation.
- Measured impact (first 3 months): Median MTTM for converted incident classes dropped from 38 minutes to 11 minutes. Operator handoff error rate reduced by 63%.

Why we ran the program

- Repeated manual steps across incidents (cache rebuilds, warmset rehydration, tiered-fallback wiring) increased cognitive load and variability.
- The operator runbook library was fragmented: inconsistent format, missing predicates, and untested commands.
- We wanted automated guardrails that are reversible and safety-checked by operators.

What we converted (example incident classes)

1) Degraded KV-prefix cache (partial corruption)
2) Model variant fallback misfire (incompatible variant served)
3) Token surge leading to quota exhaustion and throttling fallback
4) Regional capacity imbalance causing latency SLO violations

Conversion approach (high level)

1. Triage and repeatability assessment
   - For each postmortem: identify repeatable decision points, operator commands, and safety preconditions.
   - Label incident clusters with severity, frequency, and SLO impact.
2. Playbook design (template-driven)
   - Convert narrative steps into a deterministic decision DAG with: preconditions, idempotent commands, verification checks, rollout windows, and rollback criteria.
3. Automation engineering
   - Implement operator CLI wrappers + orchestration jobs (Argo Workflows or internal operator CLI) and test harnesses that simulate degraded signals.
4. Safety & review
   - Multi-team review (SRE, runtime, product) and a staged rollout (canary → limited-operator group → org-wide).
5. Metrics & telemetry integration
   - Attach SLO burn rate, Stage acceptance criteria, and post-execution telemetry to each playbook run.

Playbook template (canonical fields)

- id: short unique id (e.g. playbook.kvcache.partial-corrupt.v1)
- title: human readable title
- owner: team + pager (e.g. eng-serving-runtime, #oncall)
- severity: Sev1 | Sev2 | Sev3
- detectors: list of telemetry predicates that trigger recommendation
- preconditions: safety checks that must be true before executing an automated step
- steps: numbered steps with explicit verification checks and expected signals
- rollback: explicit rollback actions and verification
- audit: required tags, change-id, and run-notes fields
- testcases: path to synthetic scenario and acceptance criteria

Example playbook excerpt (kv-prefix cache rehydrate)

- id: playbook.kvcache.rehydrate.v1
- title: 'KV prefix cache rehydrate — partial shard corruption'
- owner: eng-serving-runtime (pager: #runtime-oncall)
- severity: Sev2
- detectors:
  - metric: runtime.kv_cache.error_rate.prefix_shard > 0.8% for 3m
  - trace sig: broken-rcu in 5% of ops across two hosts
- preconditions:
  - >= 72h since last full-shard-reshuffle (safety window)
  - no ongoing maintenance windows in target region
- steps:
  1) Run 'operator kv inspect --prefix P --shard S' to confirm bad shard nodes.
  2) If shard nodes are still alive, schedule 'operator kv partial-copy --from NODE_X --to NODE_Y --prefix P --shard S' (dry-run flag first).
  3) Verify success with 'operator kv verify --prefix P --shard S' (expect <0.1% miss rate).
  4) If verification fails, run 'operator kv rollback-copy --id ID' and notify runtime pager.
- rollback:
  - full-shard-reshuffle with live eviction safeguard; see rollback playbook id 'playbook.kvcache.full-reshuffle.v1'
- testcases:
  - synthetic scenario path: ops/synthetic/kv-rehydrate-cases/partial-corrupt-2026
  - acceptance: verification step returns <0.1% miss rate in 95% of runs

Implementation patterns and lessons learned

- Start with small, autop-run-safe steps. The biggest wins were read-only and verification automation (inspect, verify) before any mutation.
- Idempotency is mandatory. All automated mutations must include an idempotency token and an operator-observable run id. Example CLI pattern: 'operator kv partial-copy --run-id {{timestamp}} --idempotency-token {{uuid}}'.
- Safety windows and cooldowns reduced accidental double-actions. We standardized a 15-minute minimum cooldown between successive mutation steps for the same resource.
- Feature flags for automation: Each automated playbook is behind a feature flag scoped to operator groups. Rollout used a three-stage progression: off → pilot (3 operators) → team-wide → org-wide.
- Testing: For each playbook we implemented a synthetic scenario that runs nightly in the platform lab. Playbooks must pass 5 deterministic synthetic runs before licensed automation is allowed.

Key metrics we tracked

| Metric | Baseline | Post-conversion | Target |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Median MTTM (converted classes) | 38m | 11m | <=10m |
| Operator error incidence (per 100 runs) | 9.4 | 3.5 | <=2.5 |
| Playbook execution success rate | 72% | 93% | >=95% |
| Time-to-rollout (pilot → org-wide) | N/A (manual) | 18 days | <=10 days |

Operational changes we introduced

- Runbook registry: added metadata fields into service-catalog and exposed via operator CLI 'operator playbook list --service runtime'.
- Runbook schema v1.2 enforced via CI: linting, testcases, and runbook acceptance hooks in PRs.
- Playbook audit trail: every automated run emits 'playbook.run' telemetry with run_id, operator_id, and step-level timestamps. These events feed the incident-analysis pipeline.

Failures and what didn't work

- Over-automation for low-confidence decisions: Two playbooks were reverted because their detectors lacked precision, causing unnecessary evictions. Lesson: prefer recommendation-first where detectors <95% precision.
- Tooling mismatch: Early Argo-based flows required flakier network dependencies; we migrated mutation steps to the internal operator service with a lightweight task queue.
- Documentation gaps: Some playbooks assumed undocumented operational knowledge (exact CLI flags). We required embedded command examples and a short 'cheat-sheet' per playbook.

Action items (owners and timeline)

1) Incident detectors refinement: data team to add new signals for model-variant compatibility (owner: Applied ML; due: 2026-08-01).
2) Runbook schema -> v1.3: add 'confidence' field to detectors (owner: eng-platform; due: 2026-07-30).
3) Operator CLI ergonomics: reduce noisy flags and add '--dry-run --run-id' standard (owner: eng-developer-experience; due: 2026-09-15).
4) Playbook testing expansion: schedule nightly synthetic runs across 50% of playbooks (owner: platform-lab; due: 2026-08-15).
5) Rollout playbook for playbooks: create a meta-playbook that automates canary rollout steps (owner: eng-sre; due: 2026-08-05).

Decision log (selected decisions)

- D1: Prefer 'recommendation-first' for detectors with precision < 95% — approved 2026-01-10.
- D2: All mutation steps must have idempotency and run-id — approved 2025-12-20.
- D3: Nightly synthetic acceptance required before org-wide automation — approved 2026-02-04.

Runbook rollout checklist (operator playbook adopters)

1. Review detector precision (>95%) OR mark as recommendation-only.
2. Confirm preconditions (safety windows, maintenance).
3. Verify testcases have passed 5/5 synthetic runs.
4. Enable feature flag for pilot group (3 operators).
5. Run 3 supervised live runs during low-traffic window.
6. If stable, move through team-wide and org-wide stages with telemetry review after each stage.

CLI and example automation snippet

# dry-run then execute
operator playbook run --id playbook.kvcache.rehydrate.v1 --dry-run --run-id "rehydrate-2026-07-12T08:10Z"
operator playbook run --id playbook.kvcache.rehydrate.v1 --run-id "rehydrate-2026-07-12T08:10Z" --confirm

Example automation YAML (Argo-style for reference)

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  generateName: playbook-kv-rehydrate-
spec:
  entrypoint: rehydrate
  templates:
  - name: rehydrate
    steps:
    - - name: inspect
        template: inspect-task
    - - name: partial-copy
        template: partial-copy-task

(We migrated away from a heavy Argo footprint for mutation steps but keep this as a reference pattern.)

Appendix: templates and examples location

- Playbook templates repo: git+ssh://git.internal/redwood/platform/playbooks-templates (path: /templates/v1.2)
- Synthetic labs: ops-lab.redwood.internal/synthetic-playbooks/kvcache
- Acceptance dashboard: internal-grafana/d/Playbook-Acceptance/playbooks?orgId=1

Concluding notes

Converting postmortems into automated playbooks delivered measurable operational improvements and reduced cognitive load for our operators. The program highlighted the importance of detector quality, rigorous synthetic testing, and staged rollouts. The remaining work focuses on instrumentation, detector refinement, and broader operator ergonomics to ensure playbooks remain safe, reversible, and well-observed.
